messages.subject: Interpetation of combined effects
parts:
Dear all,
I made a SEM model using lavaan, where I have as exogenous variables Predation (0 or 1; absence/presence), insecticide contamination (also 0 or 1), and a Predation x insecticide variable (also 0 or 1).
I got the following standardized path coefficients:

abundance <- predation -1.13, p<0.001
abundance <- insecticide -0.48, p=0.006
abuncance <- predation x insecticide +0.421, p=0.017

How should I interpret the change of signals? why the combined effect of predation and insecticide turns on positive if the individual effects are not?

Thanks in advance,
Andreia

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Interpetation of combined effects
parts:
Andreia--
     The interaction is not a combined effect, but rather the change in effect of each predictor as the other predictor's value varies. It is common in interaction models to see these sign differences moving from main effect to interaction. To interpret, take the "simple slope" (first derivative of the regression equation) with respect to each predictor.

Simple slope (predation) = -1.13 +.42 * insecticide
Simple slope (insecticide) = -0.48 + .42 * predation

Interpreting these is easier since predation and insecticide are both 0-1. The predation simple slope means that there are two slopes for the predation effect: -1.13 when insecticide is not detected and -1.13+.42 = -.71 when insecticide is present. So predation has a stronger negative effect in those cases where insecticide is not detected.

The insecticide simple slope formula says that the slope for insecticide is -0.48 when predation is 0 and (-.48 + .42) = -.06 (or nearly 0) when predation is 1. So insecticide has almost no effect when predation is present, and predation has a lessened but still relatively large negative effect even when insecticide is present.

My go-to for interpreting interaction effects is a standard regression text like Cohen, Cohen, West and Aiken's (2003) text. It is awesomely readable.
